"""
URL: https://leetcode.com/problems/implement-magic-dictionary/description/?envType=problem-list-v2&envId=vn57k9wr

676. Implement Magic Dictionary

Design a data structure that is initialized with a list of different words. Provided a string, you should determine if you can change exactly one character in this string to match any word in the data structure.

Implement the MagicDictionary class:

- MagicDictionary() Initializes the object.
- void buildDict(String[] dictionary) Sets the data structure with an array of distinct strings dictionary.
- bool search(String searchWord) Returns true if you can change exactly one character in searchWord to match any string in the data structure, otherwise returns false.

Example 1:

Input
["MagicDictionary", "buildDict", "search", "search", "search", "search"]
[[], [["hello","leetcode"]], ["hello"], ["hhllo"], ["hell"], ["leetcoded"]]
Output
[null, null, false, true, false, false]

Explanation
MagicDictionary magicDictionary = new MagicDictionary();
magicDictionary.buildDict(["hello", "leetcode"]);
magicDictionary.search("hello"); // return False
magicDictionary.search("hhllo"); // We can change the second 'h' to 'e' to match "hello" so we return True
magicDictionary.search("hell"); // return False
magicDictionary.search("leetcoded"); // return False

Constraints:

    1 <= dictionary.length <= 100
    1 <= dictionary[i].length <= 100
    dictionary[i] consists of only lower-case English letters.
    All the strings in dictionary are distinct.
    1 <= searchWord.length <= 100
    searchWord consists of only lower-case English letters.
    buildDict will be called only once before search.
    At most 100 calls will be made to search.
"""


class MagicDictionary:

    def __init__(self):
        self.words = set()
        self.len_dict = defaultdict(list)

    def buildDict(self, dictionary: List[str]) -> None:
        self.words = set(dictionary)
        self.len_dict = defaultdict(list)
        for word in dictionary:
            self.len_dict[len(word)].append(word)

    def search(self, searchWord: str) -> bool:
        length = len(searchWord)
        if length not in self.len_dict:
            return False
        for word in self.len_dict[length]:
            diff = 0
            for c1, c2 in zip(word, searchWord):
                if c1 != c2:
                    diff += 1
                    if diff > 1:
                        break
            if diff == 1:
                return True
        return False


sol = MagicDictionary()

print(sol.buildDict(["hello", "leetcode"]))  # None
print(sol.search("hello"))  # False
print(sol.search("hhllo"))  # True
print(sol.search("hell"))  # False
print(sol.search("leetcoded"))  # False

# Using asserts for the official examples
sol = MagicDictionary()
sol.buildDict(["hello", "leetcode"])
assert sol.search("hello") == False
assert sol.search("hhllo") == True
assert sol.search("hell") == False
assert sol.search("leetcoded") == False
